learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects for machine testing.
Have adequate knowledge of machine testing, including some cutting-edge knowledge in its field within mechanical engineering.
Have the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve machine testing problems using established methods.
Have the ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in machine testing.
Have an understanding of different methods for machine testing and the ability to use them.
Have the ability to design and conduct experiments on machines, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory competences in machine testing.
Have the ability to combine theory and practice to solve problems of calculation, design, and machine testing.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in machine testing and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and perform experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competences.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while relying on advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.

syllabus_topics: Life cycle cost and machine maintenance
Machine diagnostics and fault correction techniques.
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is 30% from the final exam, 60% from assignments, and 10% from practical work. Attendance to practical sessions is mandatory and they must be passed; otherwise, students cannot take the ordinary exam. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required in the final exam for both ordinary and extraordinary calls. In the extraordinary call, the final grade will be the most favorable between Option A (same weighting as ordinary call) and Option B (100% from the final exam).
